title: LLMs as Judges and Examinees for Medical Item Difficulty Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2610.38402v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Predicting medical item difficulty from item text alone remains challenging. Prior work has largely relied on linguistic features or text representations derived from general-purpose and domain-specific language models, but predictive performance has remained modest. This study takes a different approach by using difficulty-related signals that emerge when open-weight large language models (LLMs) interact with test items. Using USMLE and PANCE medical licensure examination items, we examined LLMs in two roles. As judges, the models provided absolute difficulty ratings and pairwise difficulty comparisons. As simulated examinees, they generated response-based signals including correctness, keyed-option probability, response entropy, and the probability margin between the top two options. translated_title: 大语言模型作为裁判与考生用于医学试题难度预测
translated_abstract: 仅凭题干文本预测医学试题难度仍然具有挑战性。以往的工作主要依赖于语言学特征或源自通用型及领域专用语言模型的文本表示，但预测性能一直较为有限。本研究采取了一种不同的方法，即利用开源权重的大语言模型（LLMs）与试题交互时涌现出的难度相关信号。基于USMLE和PANCE医学执照考试题目，我们考察了大语言模型在两种角色下的表现。作为“裁判”时，模型提供绝对难度评分和两两之间的难度比较；作为“模拟考生”时，它们生成基于作答的信号，包括作答正确性、正确选项概率、作答熵以及前两个选项之间的概率差。随后，我们将最强的评判信号和作答信号与基线题目特征相结合，用于下游预测模型。两两难度判断……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究创新性地让开源大语言模型分别扮演“裁判”和“模拟考生”两种角色，提取难度评判信号与作答行为信号，并与题目基线特征结合，从而显著提升了医学试题难度的预测效果。
en_tdlr: This study innovatively employs open-weight LLMs in dual roles as judges and simulated examinees to extract difficulty-judgment and response-based signals, which, when combined with baseline item features, substantially improve medical item difficulty prediction.
